clue.text: West, South, North — after recession banks removed debit card

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress, supplies her first name
S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: recession is a moving back, so the trimmed word is read in the backward direction
the banks of a word are its outer letters, and these are taken away leaving the inside

explanation.surface: Compass points and a banking crisis: after the downturn, banks withdrew a debit card.
explanation.walkthrough: West is the Hollywood actress Mae West; 'banks' are a word's outside letters, not lenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro was the brand name of a widely used debit card scheme run by Mastercard.

clue.text: Complain about this Roman hairstyle

indicators.note: about means around, so the complaint goes round the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is Latin, the Romans' tongue, for this

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a Roman's haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' is not a Roman person: it says the word for 'this' is in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a haircut with a central strip of hair standing up and the sides shaved.

clue.text: No more endlessly sending naughty messages — about time!

indicators.note: with no ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: sexting is sending sexually explicit texts
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A cheeky plea to stop sending rude texts, and about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SEXTING to EXTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has died out completely exists no more.

clue.text: Doorkeeper runs after hat

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the hat word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A doorman chases after a hat blown away.
explanation.walkthrough: In Freemasonry the Tiler guards the lodge door; 'tile' for a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A Masonic lodge's outer guard, who keeps the door, carries this title.

clue.text: Appoint Islamic leader in Asian country (not Japan)

indicators.note: in puts that first letter inside the shortened country
not means without, so the letter for Japan is dropped

parts.note: Jordan is a country in western Asia
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern country appoints an Islamic leader, Japan excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes J from JORDAN to give ORDAN; 'in' places I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to appoint someone to a church office, or to decree.

clue.text: See 9
Marshal's phone is confiscated

indicators.note: confiscated means taken and held, so the phone word holds the little word inside it

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: An officer's phone is taken off him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' is a verb, to gather troops, not the officer; 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal forces is to assemble them ready for action, as mustering does.

clue.text: Old Indian statesman losing right to install woman as head of state

indicators.note: installing means putting in place inside, so the name goes into the shortened statesman
losing means dropping, so that letter goes

parts.note: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister
Tanya is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An Indian statesman loses office to make way for a woman leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves NEHU, and 'to install' puts the woman's name inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Netanyahu, long Israel's prime minister, heads its government.

clue.text: Percussion instruments welcome in Chinese rock

parts.note: gongs are struck percussion instruments
hi is a greeting, a welcome

explanation.surface: A Chinese band whose rock music is greeted with gongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is not music but stone.
explanation.definitionFit: These are naturally shaped stones prized and displayed by Chinese scholars.

clue.text: One can't fly after Heathrow's blocked

indicators.note: blocked means held inside, so the letters are enclosed within these words

explanation.surface: Someone stuck because Heathrow airport is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked' points to letters held in 'after Heathrow's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American bird that cannot fly, like the ostrich.

clue.text: Gareth Malone's new occupation?

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters of the name are rearranged into fresh words

explanation.surface: Imagines the TV choirmaster Gareth Malone switching careers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Malone is a British choirmaster known from television; his name supplies the twelve letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a hotel is a job, so the title of the person in charge names an occupation.

clue.text: Young socialite departs before westbound train comes in

indicators.note: the train coming in means it enters the other letters and sits between them

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tube is a London Underground train

explanation.surface: A departure board: something leaves before the westbound train arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westbound' turns the train round to EBUT, and 'comes in' sets it inside the other letters. A tube is a London Underground train.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman making her first appearance in society.

clue.text: Syrian scandal affected part of Europe

indicators.note: affected here means acted upon and altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political scandal in Syria has knock-on effects in a European region.
explanation.walkthrough: The islands lie off Africa but belong to Spain, so they count as part of Europe politically.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic archipelago is an autonomous community of Spain and so a European territory.

clue.text: Son of David Newton soon having day off

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter for day is removed

parts.note: something at hand is close by, about to happen soon

explanation.surface: A biblical genealogy entry crossed with Isaac Newton taking a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes D from AT HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the prophet's namesake Nathan is one of King David's sons born in Jerusalem.

clue.text: Girl, one with two names

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: two means the letter is written twice

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A girl known by two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a common female first name, so it serves for a girl.

clue.text: So to speak, it will be you issuing a command

indicators.note: it will be you says the word it is swapped for the word you

parts.note: as it were is a phrase meaning so to speak

explanation.surface: Someone giving an order says it will be you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' swaps IT in AS IT WERE for YOU.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the drill order telling soldiers to return to their previous position.

clue.text: At Waterloo maybe nothing's lost after absolute end of Bonaparte

indicators.note: after places the shortened station behind the abbreviation for absolute

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in degrees absolute temperature

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the zero is taken out

parts.note: Waterloo is a London railway station, an example of one
nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Napoleon at Waterloo: nothing was spared at the absolute end of Bonaparte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' is not a link word but the chemical symbol, the definition. 'lost' removes O from STATION to leave STATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: At is the chemical symbol of this rare radioactive halogen element.

clue.text: Sister is in ruins, every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A sister is in ruins, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'in ruins'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Politicians dealing with data leads to insight Cummings should be sacked

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so those letters are removed

parts.note: statistics is the science of collecting and analysing data

indicators.note: the leads of the two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A data-driven insight: Dominic Cummings, the PM's adviser, should be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes I and C from 'insight Cummings'; 'should be sacked' removes them from STATISTICS. Dominic Cummings was Boris Johnson's chief adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: Statists are politicians who favour strong central state control.

clue.text: With no European money, system must be modified by obsessive researchers

parts.note: anal is informal for obsessively fussy and precise

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
with no means lacking, so those letters are removed from the word that follows

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3

explanation.surface: Fussy researchers say a cash-strapped system needs reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' leaves SYST, which 'must be modified' rearranges to YSTS. 'obsessive' looks like it describes the researchers but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysts examine data closely, and that close study is research.

clue.text: Harass a female police officer in Paris? Close to abhorrent!

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Harassing a French policewoman would be close to abhorrent.
explanation.definitionFit: To afflict is to trouble or torment, much as harassing does.

clue.text: Coach taking on international scorer

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A football coach signs an international goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' is not a goal-getter but a composer, one who writes scores: Ferruccio Busoni.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferruccio Busoni was an Italian composer, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Talk about Desert Island Discs at noon

indicators.note: about means around, so the discs surround the other letters

parts.note: two round O letters look like discs
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A chat about the radio show Desert Island Discs at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert Island Discs' is a long-running BBC radio programme; here its words split up. 'about' puts the two Os round RAT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, a talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Evil arising in French family giving a bad reputation

indicators.note: arising means going up, and in a down clue up is to the front, so the word for evil moves to the start

parts.note: famille is French for family
ill means evil or harm

explanation.surface: Wickedness rising within a French family leaves them a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' lifts ILL from the end of FAMILLE to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is notoriety, a poor standing in people's eyes.

clue.text: Police not positive about possessing large dog

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the rearranged letters hold this one inside
about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Sceptical police deal with a large dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes P from POLICE to leave OLICE; 'about' rearranges it to COLIE; 'possessing' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a Scottish breed of sheepdog.

clue.text: Possibly what's left after a host badly abandoned his tartufo dessert?

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot, and the ones left once the host's letters are taken out are rearranged

parts.note: badly means jumbled up, and a cocktail is a mixture, so this second word tells the solver the first word's letters arrived mixed

explanation.surface: A careless dinner host leaves his tartufo half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Tartufo is an Italian ice-cream dessert. Take A HOST out of HIS TARTUFO and I R T U F are left, a mix of the first word; 'badly' says they are mixed, which is what cocktail means.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of chopped mixed fruit in syrup is a familiar sweet course.

clue.text: Boy, some like it hot!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Recalls the film title Some Like It Hot, addressed to a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith is a common male first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Dull piece of music Queen rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a number is a song or piece in a performance
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A band's song turned down by Queen, the rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the band but gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means deadened or without feeling, as dull pain or senses are.

clue.text: Entire first half of Manchester side against Real's awful

indicators.note: takes the opening three of the six letters

parts.note: Manchester United is a Premier League football club
V is short for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: awful here signals the letters being badly played, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football report: Manchester United's first half against Real Madrid was dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' gives UNI from UNITED; 'awful' rearranges REALS to ERSAL. Real is Real Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies everywhere and to everyone, so it is entire or total.

clue.text: Apple enterprise with ace location in southern Europe

parts.note: Apple products carry a lower-case i prefix, as in iPhone and iMac
biz is slang for business, an enterprise
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A tech company opens a branch at a top Mediterranean location.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean.

clue.text: Elizabeth I and II in rags

parts.note: the first and the second together are both of them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher; with two queens of that name there are two ERs

explanation.surface: Pictures the two Queens Elizabeth dressed in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rags' is a verb, to tease, not ragged clothes; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag someone is to tease or pester them, the same as to pester.

clue.text: Upgrade hospital in Cornish town without parking zone

indicators.note: in puts the hospital letter inside the shortened town
without means lacking, so these two letters are taken out

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the far south-west county of England
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Plans to improve a Cornish town's hospital with no parking zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes P and Z from PENZANCE, leaving ENANCE, and H goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to improve it, which is what upgrading does.
